item.title: Co. Roscommon school hope to reach All-Ireland final later today
item.description: A County Roscommon school will be hoping to go a step closer to an All-Ireland title later today. St Nathy's College, Ballaghaderreen will take on St Michael's College, Rosscarbery in the Schools 'B' semi-final in Limerick. The game throws in at 2 o'clock at the University of Limerick South Campus.Fr Paul Kivlehan is a member of the St Nathy's coaching staff. He says the Connacht champions are in for a tough battle: Advertisement

item.title: Revenue seize contraband worth over €135,000 in Midlands operation
item.description: Revenue officers have seized contraband worth more than one hundred and thirty-five thousand euro in a series of operations, which included the Midlands over the past week. The intelligence-led operations, which began on the sixteenth of February, resulted in the seizure of four-point-seven kilograms of herbal cannabis valued at more than ninety-four thousand euro. item.title: Protest over SNA allocations to take place in Longford Town this afternoon
item.description: A protest over SNA allocations is taking place in Longford Town this afternoon. The protest is going ahead at the Market Square despite the Government doing a U-turn on planned cuts. Similar protests took place earlier this week in Castlerea and Roscommon Town. James Donnelly is one of the organisers of the Longford Town protest: Advertisement

item.title: Strong public support at Boyle Aldi rally amid absent councillors
item.description: Hundreds gathered in Boyle this afternoon in support of the proposed new Aldi store on Patrick Street. Supporters filled The Crescent, turning out in big numbers to show their backing for the development’s future. The planned store — expected to bring jobs and investment to the area — has been appealed to An Coimisiún Pleanála, prompting the public rally. item.description: St. Nathy's College, Ballaghaderreen are sixty minutes from All-Ireland Post-Primary School's 'B' Championship glory following a terrific semi-final victory on Saturday afternoon. The Ballaghaderreen students reached the last four with a five-point triumph over The Bish of Galway a fortnight ago. item.title: Parents and carers gather in support of SNAs in Longford Town
item.description: Over a hundred people gathered in support of SNAs on Market Square in Longford Town this afternoon. Parents, carers, local representatives and SNAs themselves protested the government's review of allocations in schools across the country. Over the past number of weeks, the National Council for Special Education informed almost 200 schools nationally that their SNA allocation was being cut. item.title: Granard's Cnoc Mhuire reach All-Ireland football final
item.description: Cnoc Mhuire Granard will play St. Nathy's of Ballaghaderreen in the Masita All-Ireland Post-Primary Schools Senior 'B' Football final. That's after a comprehensive victory over Aquinas Grammar School of Belfast in Saturday's semi-final. The Granard students were in impressive form throughout scoring a goal and twenty-one points to their opponents seven. item.title: Roscommon go top of division three
item.description: Roscommon came back from the dead to rescue a point against Tyrone in Dr. Hyde Park. The Rossies looked set for their first defeat of the season before Michael Hussey’s equaliser in the fourth minute of injury time. Roscommon led 1-8 to 10 points at half-time thanks to a Cian Bowes goal nine minutes before half-time. However, Tyrone battled back and led 19-points to 1-13 on 70 minutes. item.title: Lavin claims eighth national title
item.description: Sarah Lavin (Emerald AC) claimed her eighth national indoor 60m hurdles title at the national indoor championships today. Lavin powered past of World silver heptathlon medallist Kate O’Connor (Dundalk St Gerards) who set a huge indoor personal best on her season opener. Whereas, Raheny Shamrock pair Sophie Becker and Mark Smyth dominated the 200m sprint finals.
